title: Codex vs Claude for app development
summary: Paul Hudson compares Codex and Claude through his own Apple-platform development work, favoring Codex for thorough implementation and accessibility while finding Claude useful for design ideas and debugging. He also reports overengineering and instruction-following problems; an iOS team can adopt his briefing process by having the agent question assumptions before committing a detailed plan to source control.
takeaway: Before implementation, have the agent ask clarifying questions, resolve gaps in the brief, and save the agreed plan in source control; explicitly request adversarial review where it can catch meaningful problems.
